facts.big: The sign said the shop was closed
facts.label: Said + passado
facts.sub: Para contar o que um aviso, e-mail ou mapa diz, use said + passado: The sign said the shop was closed. Não use told com avisos.

facts.label: Avisos e mensagens
facts.sub: Use said para avisos, e-mails, sites e mapas: The sign said the shop was closed. The email said the owner was sick. Depois de said, use o verbo no passado.

facts.label: Um passo atrás
facts.sub: Ao contar o que um aviso diz, o verbo volta um passo: is vira was, are vira were, will vira would. The weather report said it would be hot.

compare.ask: The sign said the shop was closed.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “o aviso dizia que a loja estava fechada”.
compare.tip: Diga: “The sign said the shop was closed.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use said + passado: “The sign said the shop was closed.” Para pessoas, use told me: He told me it was closed.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: The sign said the shop was closed.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

items.s: We say “The sign told me the shop was closed.”
items.why: Usually: The sign said the shop was closed.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: A sign can say something. → Verdadeiro (Yes: The sign said...)
We say “The sign told me the shop was closed.” → Falso (Usually: The sign said the shop was closed.)
A website can say something. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A closed shop · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a very hot Saturday morning in downtown Phoenix. The sun is already strong at eight o’clock. Dario waits at the door of a small shop. His friend Leo arrives with a cold drink. The lights inside the shop are off. Dario asks why nobody opens the door.

“Leo, why are you standing outside the shop? It opens at nine.” says Dario. “The sign on the door said the shop was closed today.” says Leo. “Strange. The website said it was open every day.” says Dario.
